title: Walk In With Your Numbers: 6 Free Tools to Give You the Edge When You Lease or Buy Commercial Property in Newcastle
excerpt: Six free tools to help Newcastle businesses compare leases, plan office space, estimate fitout costs and prepare for a property decision.
author: Your Office Space
body:
Here's how most commercial property decisions start.

Someone sends you a listing. You look at the rent. It seems fine. You book an inspection. The space looks great. Before you know it, there's a letter of offer on your desk.

And somewhere along the way, nobody asked the important questions:

- How much space do we actually need?
- What will this really cost once you add outgoings, reviews and [make-good](/blog/make-good-obligations-commercial-lease-cost)?
- What's the fitout going to set us back?
- Is this clause going to hurt us in five years?
- If we're buying, does the price stack up against the income?

The businesses that get the best outcomes are the ones who walk in prepared. They know what they need, what they can afford and what a good deal looks like. That means better conversations, faster decisions and fewer surprises down the track.

So we built the tools to help you get there. Six of them, all free, all in one place on our [Resources page](/resources).

> **No time to run the numbers yourself?** That's what we're here for. [Book a free Lease Health Check](/tenant-rep) and our tenant rep team will do it with you.

---

## Start here: which tool do you need?

| Your question | The tool | Time |
|---|---|---|
| Should we move or stay? | [Should I Relocate?](/resources/relocate-quiz) | Under 2 minutes |
| How much space do we need? | [Office Size Calculator](/resources/office-size-calculator) | 2 minutes |
| Which lease is actually cheaper? | [Lease Comparison Tool](/resources/lease-comparison) | 5 minutes |
| What's risky in our lease? | [Commercial Lease Risk Checker](/resources/lease-review) | 10 questions |
| What will the fitout cost? | [Fitout Cost Estimator](/resources/fitout-estimator) | 5 quick questions |
| Does this purchase price stack up? | [Cap Rate Calculator](/resources/cap-rate-calculator) | 5 minutes |

They're laid out in the order most businesses need them. Start at the top, or jump to the one that answers your question today.

---

## 1. Should I Relocate?

**The question it answers:** Is it time to move, or should we stay put and renegotiate?

**What you tell it:** Six quick answers about your current situation:

- When your lease expires
- How well your space fits your team
- How your rent compares to market
- Whether your headcount has changed
- How your team feels about the location
- Your main reason for thinking about a move

**What you get:** A Red, Amber or Green verdict, plus suggested next steps for your situation.

**Why it matters:** "Should we move?" is usually a gut feel. This turns it into a structured first answer in under two minutes. It's also a good one to send to your business partner or ops manager so you're having the same conversation.

[Take the Should I Relocate? quiz](/resources/relocate-quiz)

---

## 2. Office Size Calculator

**The question it answers:** How much space does our team actually need?

**What you tell it:**

- Number of staff
- Work style: traditional (everyone in daily), hybrid (50 to 70% in) or agile (30 to 50% in)
- Private offices needed
- Meeting rooms needed

**What you get:** An indicative floor area range and an indicative cost estimate.

**Why it matters:** Too much space and you're paying rent on empty desks. Too little and you're moving again in two years. Hybrid work has changed the maths, and plenty of businesses are still leasing for a team that only turns up three days a week.

[Use the Office Size Calculator](/resources/office-size-calculator)

---

## 3. Lease Comparison Tool

**The question it answers:** Which of these spaces is actually cheaper?

This is the one we wish every business owner used before signing.

**What you tell it:** For two or three options:

- Face rent ($ per m² per year)
- Area (m²)
- Lease term (years)
- Rent-free (months)
- Outgoings ($ per m² per year)
- Estimated make-good cost
- Annual rent review (%)

**What you get:**

- The true cost of each option over the lease
- A year-by-year cost breakdown
- The total in today's dollars (net present value)
- A plain-English verdict on which deal is actually cheaper

**Why it matters:** The lowest face rent is not always the cheapest lease. A building with higher rent but six months rent-free, lower outgoings and a lighter make-good can come out well ahead. You can't see that from a listing. You can see it here in about five minutes.

**Good to know:** The tool compounds rent reviews at the rate you enter, escalates outgoings at 3% a year, adds make-good at the end of the term and discounts to today's dollars at 7%.

[Compare your lease options](/resources/lease-comparison)

> **Got two offers and can't pick?** Send them to our tenant rep team. We act only for tenants, and we'll tell you which one's better and what to push for. [Start the conversation](/tenant-rep).

---

## 4. Commercial Lease Risk Checker

**The question it answers:** Which parts of our lease should we be worried about?

**What you tell it:** Ten questions about your lease. Have your lease handy, especially the sections on rent reviews, make-good and options.

**What you get:** An instant risk summary showing which topics to look at first.

**Why it matters:** Most lease problems are found when it's too late, usually at the end of the lease when the make-good bill arrives or an option date has already passed. This helps you spot the topics worth raising with your solicitor now, while you can still negotiate.

**Good to know:** The checker works from your answers only. It doesn't read your lease, and it doesn't replace your solicitor.

[Check your lease risks](/resources/lease-review)

---

## 5. Fitout Cost Estimator

**The question it answers:** What will it cost to fit out the space?

**What you tell it:** Floor area, quality level, workstation needs, any extras and your project location.

**What you get:** An indicative planning budget, including a contingency allowance. All figures are ex GST.

**Why it matters:** The [fitout](/blog/commercial-fitout-cost-newcastle-2026) is often the biggest cheque in a move, and it's the one most people underestimate. Knowing the rough number early helps you:

- Set a realistic budget before you sign a lease
- Negotiate a fitout contribution from the landlord with real numbers behind you
- Compare a space that needs a full fitout against one with a usable existing fitout

**Good to know:** It's a planning range, not a quote. Building condition, services, compliance and design can all change the final cost.

[Estimate your fitout cost](/resources/fitout-estimator)

---

## 6. Cap Rate Calculator

**The question it answers:** If we're buying, does the price stack up against the income?

**What you tell it:** Choose what you want to calculate:

- **Cap rate:** from the net operating income and the price
- **Value:** from the net operating income and a cap rate
- **Annual income:** from the price and a cap rate

There's also a helper to work out net operating income from the gross rent, vacancy allowance and the costs the owner pays.

**What you get:** The result you chose, plus "what if" scenarios at other cap rates.

**A quick example:** A property earning $90,000 a year in net income, priced at $1,500,000, is a 6% cap rate. At 7%, the same income points to a value of about $1,285,714.

**Why it matters:** Whether you're buying your own premises through an SMSF or looking at an investment, cap rate is how commercial property is compared. This lets you sense check an asking price before you get attached to the building.

**Good to know:** It's an income scenario tool, not a valuation. It doesn't cover GST, stamp duty, tax, finance or future rent changes. Get your accountant and a registered valuer involved before you rely on a number.

[Use the Cap Rate Calculator](/resources/cap-rate-calculator)

> **Thinking about buying your own premises?** Our [commercial buyers agent team](/buyers-agency) acts only for the buyer. We'll build your brief, find the right property and negotiate the price.

---

## The tools give you the numbers. We help you use them.

These tools are built to get you thinking clearly, fast. They're free, and most give you results straight away. Some ask for your name and work email to unlock a full result or report.

But a calculator can't:

- Find the space that never hits the market
- Tell you what similar spaces nearby have leased or sold for
- Negotiate a fair make-good clause
- Keep your fitout on budget once the builders start

That's what our team does. We act only for the tenant or buyer, from the first conversation through to the lease, the fitout and the furniture.

## Frequently asked questions

### Are the Your Office Space property tools free?
Yes. All six planning tools are free to use. Some ask for your name and work email to unlock a full result or report. Any tailored advice or project work is quoted separately.

### How do I compare two commercial leases?
Compare the total cost over the whole lease, not just the face rent. Include rent-free months, outgoings, annual rent reviews and the make-good cost at the end. Our free Lease Comparison Tool does this for up to three options and shows the result in today's dollars.

### How much office space do I need per person?
It depends on how your team works. A team that's in every day needs more space than a hybrid or agile team that shares desks. Private offices and meeting rooms add to the total. Our Office Size Calculator gives an indicative range based on your headcount and work style.

### How much does an office fitout cost in Newcastle?
It depends on the size of the space, the quality of the finish, the condition of the building and what's included. Our Fitout Cost Estimator gives an indicative planning budget with a contingency included. Always confirm the scope and get quotes before committing.

### What is a cap rate in commercial property?
A cap rate is the property's annual net operating income divided by its price, shown as a percentage. For example, $90,000 net income on a $1,500,000 price is a 6% cap rate. It's a quick way to compare commercial properties, but it isn't a valuation.

### Can an online tool review my commercial lease?
Not fully. Our Commercial Lease Risk Checker helps you identify which topics to look at first, based on your answers. It doesn't read your lease or replace a solicitor. Always have your solicitor review the lease before you sign.

### How do I know if I should relocate my office?
Look at your lease expiry, whether the space still fits your team, how your rent compares to market and how your team feels about the location. Our Should I Relocate? quiz turns those six factors into a Red, Amber or Green verdict with next steps.

### Are the results financial or legal advice?
No. The tools give indicative results based on the information you enter. They're planning aids, not advice. Get legal, tax and financial advice before you sign a lease or buy a property.
